summary: Import-time dropper fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated hosts
details: On require, index.js loads setup.js which selects a platform-specific asset (linux/darwin/win32), fetches an opaque binary over HTTPS from hosts reconstructed at runtime via array join (`oob-worker.cf<subdomain>.workers.dev` and `*.dl.well1.site`), writes it to /var/tmp or %TEMP% under a randomized name (`.cache_<hex>` on Unix, `dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe` on Windows impersonating a.NET diagnostic tool), chmods to 0755, executes it detached with stdio redirected to /dev/null, and unlinks after 5 seconds. A DNS-TXT fallback resolver is present as a secondary channel. Destination hostnames are split-string obfuscated to evade static inspection, and the behavior is framed in the README as opt-out telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
